title: Validate TensorView axis bindings positionally without transient name tuples
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: TensorView entry construction already requires SparseTensorEntry coordinates and TensorView axes to share the same canonical axis-name order, but it still materialized a complete tuple of TensorView axis names and then rebuilt a complete tuple of every entry's coordinate axis names solely to compare those bindings. The subsequent label validation already visited the same coordinates positionally, so the temporary name tuples duplicated work and allocation on the bounded high-cardinality entry path.
primary_claim: TensorView now validates coordinate cardinality, axis-name binding and label membership in one positional pass over the already-canonical axes and coordinates. Constructor binding validation no longer rebuilds transient axis-name tuples per entry, while exact binding refusal, deterministic entry ordering and fail-closed unknown-label behavior are preserved.
gardener_decision: Reuse the mandatory shared canonical axis ordering directly. Validate coordinate count first, then compare each coordinate axis name with the axis at the same position and validate its label against that axis. Do not retain a parallel axis-name tuple, coordinate-name tuple, cache or lookup abstraction for constructor binding checks.
acceptance: TensorView constructor binding validation does not iterate an entry solely to rebuild its axis-name tuple
exact coordinate cardinality and axis-name binding remain fail-closed
entry label membership remains fail-closed against the positionally bound canonical axis
